question: What filesystem boundary should OpenClaw expose for this request: deny-wins `tools.fs.allowedPaths`/`denyPaths`, access-mode `tools.fs.roots`, or workspace-only plus a separate exec policy split?
rationale: This defines a public config surface and security boundary, and the open implementation candidates make different compatibility, enforcement, and false-security tradeoffs.

options.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
options.body: Choose one canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging an implementation path.

options.title: Split exec into a separate tracker
options.body: Allow a file-tool-only policy only if docs and labels clearly state that shell-mediated file access remains a separate boundary.

options.title: Defer host path ACLs
options.body: Keep only `workspaceOnly` and sandbox backends if maintainers decide OpenClaw should not own host filesystem path policy beyond those existing controls.

recommendation.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
recommendation.body: Choose one canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging an implementation path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current schema/tool-policy history and previously framed this issue as the canonical security-boundary decision.
